_comment: Cross-language conformance cases for rendering a spare quantity. Home Keeper formats these numbers twice: in Python (assets.format_quantity) for the line it puts on a household's shopping list, and in TypeScript (utils.formatQuantity) for the panel and the dashboard card. A household reading '500 ml' in the panel must not find '500.0 ml' on their list, so both implementations run these cases and must agree on every one. The halfway values are the interesting ones: Python's round() breaks a tie to the even digit while JavaScript's toFixed breaks it away from zero, which is a real divergence the Python side quantizes around. value is the number, unit is the label beside it ('' for a part that counts whole spares), expected is the rendered string.

cases.name: a whole count keeps no decimal point
a whole float is still a whole count
a measured part names its unit
a half reads as a half
float noise never reaches the shopper
below three places rounds to nothing
a blank unit is no unit
